mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when UNRATE > 4.5 is positive in more than 60% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings growth expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages is negative in more than 60% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when INDPRO declines during late-cycle expansion is positive in more than 60% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) signals robust residential construction activity, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 5-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.0% signals monetary tightening, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when FEDFUNDS > 1.0 is positive in more than 60% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2pp and a decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) below 0.1% signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS growth rate < 0.1%
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS growth rate < 0.1% is positive in more than 60% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when INDPRO rises during early-cycle expansion is negative in more than 60% of observations.
